covers.quote: Write most direct speech in single quote marks.
Use them to:
show direct speech and the quoted work of other writers
Double quotation marks aren’t Australian Government style. Use them only for quotations within quotations.
Short quotations of direct speech are enclosed in single quotation marks.
For quotations within quotations, use double quotation marks inside single ones.
If the US material uses the US conventions for quotation marks, you can update them to the Australian convention.

rules.quote: Quote direct speech in single quote marks
rules.violation_condition: Short direct speech or quoted writing lacks quotation marks, outer quotation marks are double rather than single, or a quotation within single quotation marks uses single rather than double quotation marks.
when: Use single quotation marks for ordinary quotations and double quotation marks for quotations within them.
Long quotations use block formatting instead of enclosing quotation marks.
Speech in transcripts and plays does not need quotation marks when the speaker’s name precedes it; questions and answers have the same exception.
US quotation-mark conventions in quoted US material may be retained or updated to Australian conventions.
Separate rules govern the boundaries of quotations continuing over several paragraphs and whether titles require quotation marks.
rules.why: G-2 combines ordinary and nested quotation-mark conventions and records exceptions; G-4 absorbs repeated statements.

rules.quote: If you use ellipses for omitted words, ensure that the omission won’t mislead readers about the content or tone of the source you’re quoting.
rules.violation_condition: An omission from quoted speech misrepresents the source’s content or tone, including an unmarked omission that misleadingly presents an incomplete statement as complete.
when: Words have been omitted from quoted direct speech.
Assess the quotation against its source, not merely the grammatical acceptability of the shortened text.
rules.why: G-1 selects the actionable body instruction rather than the grouping heading; the examples establish that omission can mislead through missing words or missing indication of omission.

rules.quote: If the quotation needs the information for context, add specific detail in square brackets.
rules.violation_condition: A quotation lacks specific contextual information necessary to understand what the speaker meant or referred to.
when: The quotation needs additional information for context.
Formatting and accuracy of supplied information are checked separately.
rules.why: The grain test separates missing necessary context from incorrectly formatted or inaccurate additions.

covers.quote: add specific detail in square brackets.

rules.quote: If you paraphrase omitted material, place the paraphrasing in square brackets.
rules.violation_condition: Contextual detail inserted into a quotation, or a paraphrase substituted for omitted material, is not enclosed in square brackets.
when: The words are supplied by the quoting writer as contextual detail or as a paraphrase of omitted material.
This does not require brackets around words that were actually spoken or written in the source.
rules.why: G-2 combines two conditions requiring the same square-bracket check; the grain test keeps this separate from contextual completeness and accuracy.

rules.quote: You must be sure that the specific detail is correct and that it retains the meaning intended by the original speaker.
rules.violation_condition: Specific detail added to a quotation is factually incorrect or changes the meaning intended by the original speaker.
when: Specific detail has been added to a quotation to provide context.
rules.why: This states a required property of the added text, not merely a checking workflow; its accuracy check is distinct from the square-bracket check.

rules.quote: To show the error is in the original, insert an italicised ‘sic’ in non-italicised square brackets after the error.
rules.violation_condition: An annotation identifying an error as belonging to the quoted original is not an italicised ‘sic’ in non-italicised square brackets immediately after the error.
when: The writer is identifying a spelling or grammatical error as present in the original quoted material.
The instruction specifies how to identify an original error; it does not expressly require every original error to be annotated.
rules.why: G-2 retains the annotation’s wording, typography and placement as one convention, conditional on identifying an original error.

rules.quote: In quoted material use the original spelling of the quoted material, even if it uses US spellings such as ‘color’.
rules.violation_condition: A word in quoted material has had its original spelling changed, including conversion of a US spelling to an Australian spelling.
when: The text is presented as quoted material rather than a paraphrase.
Compare spelling with the original source.
rules.why: The grain test distinguishes spelling preservation from the separately stated mandatory capitalisation requirement.

rules.quote: The capitalisation of words must also be the same as in the original.
rules.violation_condition: A word in quoted material has different capitalisation from the original source.
when: The text is presented as quoted material rather than a paraphrase.
Compare capitalisation with the original source.
rules.why: This is an explicit mandatory requirement, separate from the preceding bare instruction about spelling.

covers.quote: For long quotes, use block quotations without quotation marks.
Don’t use quotation marks for long quotations. Instead, use block quotations.
Quotations that are longer than about 30 words are:
usually indented from the text margin
sometimes set in a smaller font size or a different font.
Don’t use quotation marks to identify the quoted material – the formatting does that instead.

rules.quote: Format long quotes as block quotations with no quotation marks
rules.specification: For an operational length threshold, treat more than 30 words as long. This is a chosen interpretation of ‘longer than about 30 words’, not an exact threshold stated by the manual. Block quotations themselves should not have enclosing quotation marks, regardless of length.
rules.violation_condition: A long quotation is presented as ordinary inline text rather than a block quotation, or a block quotation has enclosing quotation marks.
when: The manual describes long quotations as longer than about 30 words.
Block quotations are usually indented; a smaller or different font is optional.
Consecutive paragraphs of quoted speech presented using the separately described continuing-speech convention are a distinct case.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the repeated block-quotation convention; E-4 makes the chosen length threshold explicit.

covers.quote: at the beginning of each paragraph
at the end of the last paragraph only.

rules.quote: To include several paragraphs of quoted speech without the attribution tag, such as in a media release, use a quotation mark:
rules.violation_condition: Continuing quoted speech lacks an opening quotation mark at the beginning of a paragraph or a closing mark at the end of the last paragraph, or has a closing mark at the end of a non-final paragraph.
when: One speaker’s quoted speech continues over several paragraphs without a repeated attribution tag.
Put an opening quotation mark at the beginning of every paragraph.
Put a closing quotation mark only at the end of the last paragraph.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the opening and closing boundaries of a continuing multi-paragraph quotation together as one convention.

covers.quote: Quotation marks are unnecessary in transcripts and plays if the name of the speaker comes before the direct speech.
The same applies for questions and answers (Q&As).

rules.quote: Write speech in transcripts and plays with no quotation marks
rules.violation_condition: Speech preceded by the speaker’s name in a transcript or play, or a labelled question or answer in a Q&A, is enclosed in quotation marks.
when: In transcripts and plays, the speaker’s name comes before the direct speech.
The same convention applies to questions and answers in Q&As.
rules.why: G-2 combines transcripts, plays and Q&As as cases of the same no-quotation-marks convention; G-4 absorbs the body restatement.

covers.quote: Refer to certain kinds of titles using quotation marks
enclose the title of certain works
a chapter in a book or report
an article in a periodical
an essay
a lecture
a poem
a song.

rules.quote: When referring to these titles, use quotation marks in references and citations:
rules.violation_condition: A referenced or cited title of a chapter, periodical article, essay, lecture, poem or song lacks enclosing quotation marks.
when: The title is that of a chapter in a book or report, an article in a periodical, an essay, a lecture, a poem or a song.
The page’s example includes a title referred to in running text.
The general quotation-mark convention determines whether the marks are single or nested double marks.
rules.why: G-2 treats the listed title types as conditions of one check; G-4 selects the more specific body instruction.

covers.quote: If the punctuation mark is part of the quoted text, place the punctuation mark before the closing quotation mark.
The same rule applies for directly quoted speech followed by the attribution.
If the punctuation mark is part of the sentence outside the quoted text, it follows the closing quotation mark.
In these cases, place the quotation marks inside the sentence punctuation.
If the quotation ends a sentence or is a sentence in its own right, place the final full stop before the final quotation mark.

rules.quote: Keep quoted punctuation marks in the quote
rules.specification: Read the instruction about a quotation ending a sentence as applying to complete quoted sentences or direct speech. A quoted fragment integrated into the surrounding sentence takes the surrounding sentence’s punctuation outside, as the page’s examples show.
rules.violation_condition: A punctuation mark belonging to quoted material is outside its closing quotation mark, or punctuation belonging to the surrounding sentence is incorrectly inside the quotation marks.
when: Punctuation belonging to the quoted text goes before its closing quotation mark.
Punctuation belonging to the surrounding sentence goes after the closing quotation mark.
Direct speech followed by an attribution keeps its speech punctuation inside the quotation marks.
For parenthetical quoted material, quotation marks sit inside the enclosing parentheses, dashes or commas.
A complete quoted sentence or sentence-ending direct quotation takes its final full stop inside the closing quotation mark.
A separate rule governs competing terminal punctuation marks.
rules.why: G-2 combines inside and outside placement as cases of one punctuation-position check; the interpretation reconciles the full-stop wording with the examples.

covers.quote: Sometimes, there are 2 punctuation marks – one for the quotation and one for the sentence.

rules.quote: Decide which is stronger and use it. Don’t use both punctuation marks.
rules.specification: The examples establish that a quoted exclamation mark displaces an enclosing sentence’s full stop, and an enclosing question mark displaces a quoted full stop. The page does not provide a complete ordering of punctuation strength.
rules.violation_condition: A quotation boundary retains both competing terminal punctuation marks, or retains the weaker mark instead of the stronger one.
when: Both the quotation and its surrounding sentence would otherwise supply terminal punctuation at the same boundary.
rules.why: The grain test separates selecting one terminal mark from deciding which side of the quotation boundary it occupies.

covers.quote: If the content inside the quotation marks is in italics, but the sentence is in roman, use roman for the quotation marks.

rules.quote: The surrounding text determines the font (roman, italic, or bold) of the quotation marks.
rules.violation_condition: Quotation marks use a roman, italic or bold style inconsistent with the surrounding text, including taking the style of the quoted words instead.
when: Determine the quotation marks’ style from the surrounding text, not from differently styled content inside the marks.
rules.why: G-4 combines the general typography requirement and its specific italic-content example.

rules.why: G-4 combines the general typography requirement and its specific italic-content example.
